channel.title: Security Brief
channel.description: Original analysis and ranked cybersecurity news with links to original sources

item.title: The edge is where attackers get in: this week's firewall, VPN and remote-access exploits
item.description: Five exploited flaws in firewalls, VPNs, remote-support software and file-sharing servers show one pattern. The systems that sit at the edge of your network, and that administrators manage remotely, are the weakest link. Here is what to check first.

item.title: October 2026 Patch Tuesday: what the Microsoft feed shows and what to do
item.description: The Microsoft feed lists few entries, and most of them are updates to October's release rather than new fixes. The one item that needs planning is a .NET remote code execution flaw that Microsoft has not fixed yet. Identity Web and WSL need version checks if you use them.

item.title: Weekly M365 & Entra Briefing: 13 to 19 October 2026
item.description: Exchange sign-in problems after October Windows Server updates, an identity-based incident at ConnectWise that affected Microsoft 365 tenants, and why device-code abuse is still worth a Conditional Access check.

item.title: CISA Flags SonicWall SonicOS MFA Bypass Flaw Amid Reports of Possible Exploitation
item.description: The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) has added a high-severity vulnerability impacting SonicWall SonicOS to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, following reports that it said may have been exploited in real-world attacks. The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-19868 (CVSS…

item.title: CISA flags Cisco BroadWorks flaw as actively exploited in attacks
item.description: The US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) warned on Tuesday that hackers are now exploiting a high-severity Cisco BroadWorks vulnerability in attacks.

item.title: New worm-like 'SCKit' malware targets MSPs in ScreenConnect attacks
item.description: A new worm-like malware toolkit named SCKit was deployed in the recent ScreenConnect attacks targeting managed service providers (MSPs), designed to spread from infected customer devices to MSP technicians' computers and compromise additional managed networks.

item.title: IBM Aspera Faspex, SignalWire FreeSwitch Vulnerabilities Exploited in Attacks
item.description: CISA has added CVE-2026-123218 and CVE-2026-116779 to KEV, urging federal agencies to patch them within three days. The post IBM Aspera Faspex, SignalWire FreeSwitch Vulnerabilities Exploited in Attacks appeared first on SecurityWeek.

item.title: CVE-2026-111497 Google: CVE-2026-111497 Buffer overflow vulnerability in the Brotli decoder
item.description: Updated the Security Updates table to include affected Windows versions and the applicable November 2026 security updates. Microsoft recommends that customers install the applicable updates to be protected from this vulnerability.

item.title: Microsoft Fixes Nearly 1,100 Security Vulnerabilities
item.description: Microsoft did another four-digit patch drop today, releasing updates to fix almost 1,100 security vulnerabilities in its Windows operating systems and supported software. This month’s Patch Tuesday addresses 63 critical flaws — including a zero-day in Microsoft Outlook — and comes amid important security updates from…

item.title: November Patch Tuesday: An Overflowing Cornucopia of CVEs
item.description: Microsoft serves up an actively exploited Outlook zero-day, and a wave of critical Exchange, SharePoint, Windows Search, and LDAP bugs that exhausted defenders need to prioritize fast.

item.title: Kazakhstan-linked hackers used AI agent to spy on Central Asian governments
item.description: Suspected Kazakhstan-linked hackers used an artificial intelligence agent to help spy on Central Asian governments, steal sensitive documents and infiltrate critical infrastructure networks, according to new research.

item.title: Critical Xen Orchestra Flaws Exploited in Attacks
item.description: A critical authentication bypass allows attackers to execute arbitrary code as admin and take over XCP-ng nodes. The post Critical Xen Orchestra Flaws Exploited in Attacks appeared first on SecurityWeek.

item.title: Hackers exploit SSHole OpenSSH flaw to breach Linux systems
item.description: Hackers are actively exploiting the "SSHole" vulnerability (CVE-2026-123158) in OpenSSH to execute commands, steal credentials, and establish persistent access.

item.title: Microsoft 365 Outage Disrupts Outlook, Exchange Online and Teams
item.description: Microsoft says failed server health checks disrupted Outlook and other Microsoft 365 services. The company is still investigating the cause and has disclosed no evidence of a cyberattack. The post Microsoft 365 Outage Disrupts Outlook, Exchange Online and Teams appeared first on SecurityWeek.

item.title: Apify rotates API tokens, prompts 2FA resets after breach
item.description: Apify has rotated critical internal secrets and revoked some third-party OAuth connections after detecting unauthorized access to its internal systems.

item.title: CVE-2026-120792 Aspire Information Disclosure Vulnerability
item.description: Updated the products listed in the Security Updates table. This is an informational change only.

item.title: Threat Actors Exploit Openwave, Cisco BroadWorks Vulnerabilities
item.description: The flaws, CVE-2026-111793 and CVE-2026-20320, let attackers leak sensitive information, including configuration data. The post Threat Actors Exploit Openwave, Cisco BroadWorks Vulnerabilities appeared first on SecurityWeek.

item.title: Microsoft November 2026 Patch Tuesday fixes 1,235 flaws, Outlook zero-day
item.description: Today is Microsoft's November 2026 Patch Tuesday, with security updates addressing a record-breaking 1,235 flaws, including one actively exploited Microsoft Outlook zero-day vulnerability.

item.title: Hackers Exploit Critical Xen Orchestra Auth Bypass Flaw to Gain Admin Access
item.description: French software company Vates VMS has warned of a critical security vulnerability in Xen Orchestra that it said is being actively exploited in the wild. item.title: Critical Xen Orchestra auth bypass flaw exploited to hijack VM servers
item.description: A critical authentication bypass vulnerability in Xen Orchestra is being actively exploited in attacks that could grant administrator privileges and allow takeover of XCP-ng virtualization hosts.

item.title: Apache Patches Critical HTTP Server RCE Found by Anthropic, Google
item.description: The mod_http2 race condition, CVE-2026-119618, could let unauthenticated attackers execute code on servers with HTTP/2 enabled. The post Apache Patches Critical HTTP Server RCE Found by Anthropic, Google appeared first on SecurityWeek.

item.title: Inside an AI Attack Against a US Retailer
item.description: When hand-typed commands failed to breach a US retailer, the attacker turned to AI-generated scripts, achieving lateral movement in minutes.

item.title: Maersk confirms data breach as WhiteArmor ransomware demands $5 million
item.description: Maersk announced that a threat actor gained unauthorized access to a local legacy system inherited through an earlier acquisition and extracted data from it.

item.title: CVE-2026-105588 Windows DHCP Server Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability
item.description: Missing authentication for critical function in Windows DHCP Server allows an authorized attacker to elevate privileges locally.

item.title: Google patches eighth Chrome zero-day exploited in attacks this year
item.description: Google has released emergency security updates to patch a new Chrome vulnerability exploited in zero-day attacks, the eighth such flaw since the start of the year.

item.description: Dubbed 4EverAble2Shell, the flaw could allow remote, unauthenticated attackers to execute code with root privileges. The post Hackers Exploit New N-central Zero-Day Hours After PoC Publication appeared first on SecurityWeek.

item.title: Extortion Group Luna Moth Flits Into Law Firms a Second Time
item.description: The cybercriminals are retargeting law firms that refused to pay its first ransom, with a social engineering con aimed at stealing Microsoft access tokens.

item.title: New N-able "4EverAble2Shell" zero-day exploited hours after PoC released
item.description: Hackers are actively exploiting a newly disclosed N-able N-central zero-day vulnerability dubbed "4EverAble2Shell" to compromise servers and deploy cryptocurrency miners, with researchers reporting at least 21 affected systems, including 19 running the company's latest security update.

item.title: Apache HTTP Server patches critical HTTP/2 remote code execution flaw
item.description: A critical vulnerability in the HTTP/2 module of Apache HTTP Server could be exploited by an unauthenticated attacker to obtain remote code execution (RCE).

item.title: Shipping giant Maersk says recent cyber incident affected legacy system
item.description: The incident is the latest in a string of attacks on ports and other shipping organizations worldwide, with Brazil’s largest port hit with ransomware last week.

item.title: New SignDrop Zero-Day Exploit Turns Windows CLFS Security Feature Into SYSTEM Access
item.description: Public exploit code released earlier this week claims that a local Windows user can gain SYSTEM privileges through the Common Log File System driver. item.title: Critical Red Hat Quay Flaw Lets Attackers Read and Overwrite All Private Container Images in a Registry
item.description: A critical flaw in Red Hat Quay allows an attacker who can access a Quay registry to read and overwrite private container images in every repository. Quay enables anonymous access by default, and while it is enabled, the attacker needs no account. When it is off, anyone with a valid account can still exploit the flaw…

item.title: ConnectWise investigates ScreenConnect breaches after reports of incidents at nearly 50 organizations
item.description: Abuse of an independent third-party tool led to breaches at ScreenConnect customers, confirmed the software's maker, ConnectWise. Cybersecurity researchers had spotted intrusions at nearly 50.

item.title: New Windows SignDrop zero-day gives hackers SYSTEM privileges
item.description: Security researcher Abdelhamid Naceri (also known as Nightmare Eclipse) has released a new Windows zero-day exploit that can let attackers gain SYSTEM privileges.
